newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down in lower volume on Friday ahead of a five-day holiday, traders said.
Both the T-bill repo and spot market will close from Saturday to next Wednesday due to the National Day holiday.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract plunged to 7.13 percent from 24.40 percent on Thursday.
Turnover shrank to 4.95 million lots from 11.44 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"Many institutions withdrew from trading due to the long holiday," said one trader. "The market trend after the holiday will depend on the performance of the domestic A share market."
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up, with liquidity flowing into the market after prices had fallen for weeks before a technical rebound on Wednesday.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 closed slightly up at 120.91 yuan from 120.90 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose to 2.78 million lots from 2.23 million on Thursday.

"The 10-year contract is regarded as the barometer of the market and its rise today means that market sentiment is improving," said one trader. "New funds seem to have entered the market and investors began to build large positions today."
Traders expect the rates to further recover in the short term right after the holiday.
